name: Field Doctor-Style Red Pesto + Roasted Vegetable Penne (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
650 g Penne Pasta (GLUTEN FREE) [brown rice flour]
1 x 400 g tin Plum Tomato
1 1/2 medium Aubergines
3 1/2 medium Carrots
1 medium Courgette
125 g Extra Virgin Olive Oil
1/2 Red Peppers
55 g Tomato Puree [tomato]
47 g Kalamata Olives [olives, water, salt, red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil]
47 g Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
37 g Fennel
29 g Chives
27 g Sundried Tomatoes [Sundried tomatoes, Salt]
4 tbsp Sweet Noble Paprika
5 tbsp Parsley Flat
5 tbsp Mixed Herbs
1 1/2 tbsp Tapioca Starch
2 tsp Sea Salt
1 1/2 tbsp Fennel Ground
1 tbsp Black Pepper
directions:
1. Roast veg: Toss aubergine, courgette, carrot and red pepper with olive oil, salt and pepper. Roast at 200°C until soft and coloured.

2. Pasta: Boil gluten-free brown-rice penne until al dente; drain, keeping a little cooking water.

3. Red pesto-style sauce: Warm olive oil with chives and fennel. Add chopped tomato, tomato puree, sundried tomatoes, olives, sweet paprika, fennel ground, herb mix and a splash of water. Simmer until thick; stir in tapioca slurry if needed. Blitz partly for a pesto-like texture or leave rustic.

4. Combine: Toss pasta with sauce and roasted vegetables. Finish with hard cheese, parsley, salt and black pepper.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Red Pesto + Roasted Vegetable Penne (Low FODMAP) (~369 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/provencal-vegetable-pasta
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~369 g x 8 = 2952 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~540 g (inferred ~18.31% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Extra Virgin Olive Oil is kept as an ingredient on this recipe because the ready meal is relatively oil-rich (or pesto-style); still fry/roast in extra virgin olive oil as directed.
